primary_meaning: A forensic or legal declaration by God whereby a sinner is declared righteous, acquitted of guilt, and granted right standing before God, typically through faith in Jesus Christ (historic Protestant view).

alternatives.meaning: A transformative process where an individual is intrinsically made righteous through the infusion of God's grace and active participation in good works (historic Roman Catholic view).

An ecclesiological and covenantal declaration that identifies who belongs to the covenant family of God, rather than merely a soteriological mechanism for dealing with individual guilt (New Perspective on Paul).
A therapeutic process of healing and participation in the divine nature (Theosis or Deification), emphasizing organic union with Christ over forensic courtroom metaphors (Eastern Orthodox view).

notes: While all major Christian traditions agree that justification results in a restored relationship with God, there is no single settled consensus on the theological mechanics. The historic divide between Protestant (forensic/declarative) and Roman Catholic (transformative/infused) interpretations remains foundational, alongside modern scholarly debates such as the New Perspective on Paul.
